35/S0.subgoal: Describe the role of requirement gathering in the interactive system development life cycle as the stage where end-user usability requirements are identified.

35/S1.subgoal: Distinguish system-centered design from user-centered design by whose needs drive the design.

35/S2.subgoal: Identify end-user usability requirements as distinct from feasibility, interface design, and code design decisions using a calendar app example.

35/S3.subgoal: Explain usability requirements as non-functional interface-quality requirements relevant to interactive systems used by non-experts.

35/S4.subgoal: Describe the contextual inquiry method, including why requirement gathering must start from specified users and a specified context of use according to the ISO usability definition.

35/S5.subgoal: Explain why contextual inquiry is important for system development by showing how observed user activities determine essential features.

35/S6.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture.
